title: Reporting and the 13-week cash forecast
goal: Produce Juan's weekly brief and a rolling 13-week cash forecast with every assumption written down.
skills: Cash vs profit vs available cash
concept_card: Company cash, project cash, profit and available cash are different numbers. A forecast line is either known (in the books or signed) or an estimate with a written assumption. If a number has no source, it goes in the brief as “unknown.”
lesson_html:
Four different numbers. Keep them separate on every report:

  • Company cash: the bank balance of one company
  • Project cash: money spent and received on one property
  • Profit: income minus cost; a flip can be profitable while cash is low
  • Available cash: cash you can spend after bills due, loan payments and restricted funds

13-week cash forecast. One row per week:

Starting cash + money coming in − money going out = Ending cash

Money in: house sales, lender draws, plumbing customer payments. Money out: bills due, payroll, loan payments, rehab spending. Label each line as known (signed, scheduled) or estimate, and write down the assumption. Update it every week and compare last week's forecast with what really happened.

The weekly brief for Juan answers eight questions: cash today, lowest cash in the next 13 weeks, money owed to us, bills due, projects over budget, lender draws pending, open exceptions, and three decisions he needs to make.
rule: If a number has no source, it doesn't go in the brief. Write "unknown" instead.

qbo_steps.title: Aging reports
qbo_steps.html: Reports → A/R Aging Summary and A/P Aging Summary for each company.

qbo_steps.title: Cash position
qbo_steps.html: Reports → Balance Sheet (cash accounts) or the bank account list on the dashboard. Use reconciled balances where possible.

qbo_steps.title: Upcoming bills
qbo_steps.html: Reports → Unpaid bills, sorted by due date.

qbo_steps.title: Export for the forecast
qbo_steps.html: Export each report to Excel (the export icon at the top of any report). Build the forecast in one spreadsheet with a tab per company, formulas visible.

qbo_steps.title: Save report settings
qbo_steps.html: Customize a report once and click Save customization so you run the same version every week.

scenario.text_html: Peninsula Plumbing has $60,000 cash today. Week 1: pays $25,000. Week 2: pays $30,000. Week 3: receives a $45,000 customer payment and pays $10,000.
scenario.ask: What is the lowest ending cash across these three weeks?
scenario.explain: Week 1 ends at $35,000. Week 2 ends at $5,000. Week 3 ends at $40,000. The low point is $5,000 at the end of week 2. Flag it to Juan now, with options such as moving a payment or confirming the customer payment date.
scenario.followup: A customer promised to pay next week but has missed two promises. Is that payment known or an estimate?

quiz.q: A flip shows $40,000 profit but the company's cash barely moved. Most likely why?
options: Sale proceeds paid off the loan, and costs were paid earlier
Profit and cash are always equal
quiz.why: Profit and cash are different. Loan payoff and timing explain most gaps.
quiz.followup: The forecast assumes a house sells on Nov 20 for $385,000. What happens to the lowest-cash week if it slips 4 weeks?

quiz.q: A forecast line depends on a sale that hasn't closed. How do you show it?
options: As an estimate with the assumption written down
Leave it out entirely without a note
quiz.why: Label estimates and state the assumption (closing date, price) so Juan knows the risk.

quiz.q: A customer invoice is 95 days overdue. What do you do?
options: Follow up, flag it in the brief, and ask the CPA about collectability
quiz.why: Old receivables need action and may not be collectible.

quiz.q: Juan asks for total cash across all four companies. You…
options: Show each company's cash separately, then a total labeled as not all available
Move all cash into one company
quiz.why: Each company's cash belongs to that company. A total is fine only when labeled.

quiz.q: The forecast shows cash going negative in week 6. When do you tell Juan?
options: Now, in this week's brief with options
quiz.why: The point of a forecast is early warning. Give him options while there's time.

task: Build a 13-week cash forecast for one company and write Juan's weekly brief. Every number cites its report and date.
rubric: Starting cash ties to reconciled balance
Every line labeled known or estimate with an assumption
Brief answers all eight questions and lists three decisions
